held_valid_exact_grace.interpretation: An unchanged ingress valid held after its handshake is accepted once and grace-suppressed.

whole_descriptor_replay.interpretation: After a sampled-low gap and bank recycle, the same base/context/key/row descriptor is a second legal transaction; no sequence ID deduplicates an upstream retry.

m119_p0_closure.interpretation: M121 closes the standalone mapper ownership ambiguity only at the directed service handshake cut, exactly as its narrow paper statement says; it does not close application-level retry/replay.

findings.finding: scheduler_protocol_error is ORed into the top protocol_error but is not propagated into the numeric island and does not gate accumulator_window_end_ready/accept or commit_valid. Independent commercial VCS first accumulated a legal event, then injected an out-of-range scheduler request: top protocol_error became sticky while numeric_protocol_error stayed low, yet window_end was accepted and commit_valid asserted under the combined fault.
findings.impact: The architecture claim that scheduler and numeric failures are sticky and combined fail-closed is false. A downstream consumer following commit_valid can consume partial data after the scheduler has aborted remaining descriptor work.
findings.required_action: Create a sticky top-level composite fault/abort state. On any scheduler or numeric fault, block new window_start/window_end acceptance and suppress commit_valid until reset or an explicitly verified abort protocol completes. Older accepted internal writes may drain only behind the external quarantine. Add SVA that protocol_error implies no window-end accept and no commit_valid, plus a directed fault-after-accepted-update regression.

findings.finding: M117 exact grace suppresses an unchanged valid held across one handshake, but after a sampled-low gap and descriptor-bank recycle, an identical base/context/key/row descriptor is accepted and accumulated again with no fault. Independent VCS observed two accepts, six loads, two events and two updates.
findings.impact: The M119 exact-once P0 is closed only for the directed scheduler-generated service sequence, not for application-level descriptor retry/replay. The contract correctly keeps heldout duplicate/retry/escape replay false.
findings.required_action: Carry an upstream descriptor/event sequence ID or epoch and prove planned, accepted, accumulated and committed identities one-to-one over retry/reset recovery.

findings.finding: weight_rd_data has no response_valid, returned key/beat, error or latency handshake. The mapper unconditionally interprets the next cycle as the response and tail-bypasses current weight_rd_data for beat2.
findings.impact: With an otherwise legal two-cycle memory model, all token/read/update counters remained correct and protocol_error stayed low, but lane0 was 0 instead of -128 and lane95 was -93 instead of 67.
findings.required_action: Freeze a macro-backed fixed-latency response contract with timing assertions, or add response_valid/key/beat and hold the event until beat2 identity is verified.

findings.finding: M117 generates service_destination_row and context-qualified prefetch identity, but M121 feeds only row_offset to M120; the weight read request carries only seven-bit key plus beat. The production test uses two different bases/contexts while its weight oracle depends only on key and its accumulator reference aliases both descriptors into the same local rows.
findings.impact: The directed numeric miter does not prove context-dependent weight residency, destination-window attribution or non-aliasing across real descriptors.
findings.required_action: Freeze a same-output-window/same-weight-residency invariant, or carry context/window identity through weight response and commit; assert the destination-row-to-local-row mapping.

findings.finding: The production positive run reports zero numeric downstream backpressure cycles. M117/M120 treat several valid-while-not-semantically-ready conditions as sticky faults rather than conventional valid-held backpressure.
findings.impact: The composed interface has not demonstrated payload stability, liveness and no duplicate/skip across numeric stalls or early window-end valid. An external producer must be credit/semantic-ready qualified.
findings.required_action: Freeze the nonstandard fail-fast producer contract or add skid/credit adapters, then inject long scheduler, mapper, accumulator and window-end stalls.

findings.finding: descriptor_done is emitted when the scheduler accepts the final event, before that event has necessarily passed mapper and accumulator write stages. M121 does not generate a numeric-drained/window-end-safe pulse; the production TB waits on internal scheduler/numeric signals procedurally.
findings.impact: A consumer cannot equate descriptor_done with safe accumulator end or commit. Incorrect timing produces a numeric protocol fault or partial completion.
findings.required_action: Expose a public composed drain/retirement acknowledgement or internally sequence descriptor completion through final accumulator write before permitting window_end.

findings.finding: The positive test is two synthetic dense descriptors with algorithmic key-only weights and alternating negate. It does not replay frozen heldout PWP anchor/correction/escape records, duplicates or retries.
findings.impact: The signed19 exact-once premise and real workload address/order coverage remain unadmitted, as the contract correctly states.

findings.finding: Weight and lane memories remain behavioral, prefetch is always ready, and no shared arbiter/bank conflicts, foundry macros, STA/PTPX or matched baseline are present.
findings.impact: The 2.53546204172554x value remains an unadmitted M109 software projection, not RTL-measured, physical, system or headline speedup. M121 states this boundary correctly.

findings.finding: The SVA checks only protocol_error equality; it does not assert that a combined fault suppresses window-start/end acceptance, service consumption or commit visibility.
findings.suggested_action: Add explicit sticky quarantine and post-fault no-consume/no-commit assertions.

findings.finding: The sealed run's only protocol attack closes a descriptor without starting an accumulator window. It does not attack duplicate ingress, load/event mismatch, latency, descriptor transitions, reset, fault-after-consumption or corrupt data with conserved counts.
findings.suggested_action: Promote the independent counterexamples and a full malformed matrix into a new production regression.

findings.finding: Counts prove 98,304 event accepts and updates but do not carry a unique descriptor/event ID through scheduler, mapper, accumulator write and commit.
findings.impact: A duplicate plus a drop can keep counts equal; delayed-response corruption already demonstrates that correct counts do not imply correct data outside the one-cycle oracle.

findings.finding: Synchronous reset clears scheduler descriptors, mapper payload/update state and accumulator valid bits without an abort receipt or epoch handoff; reset is tested only between phases.
findings.suggested_action: Declare reset as destructive abort requiring upstream replay with a new epoch, and test reset at load0/load2/event/update/write/commit boundaries.

findings.finding: Ingress already contains unique dense descriptor events. PWP selection, correction/escape construction, duplicate removal, source trace delivery and their cost are outside M121.
findings.impact: The directed island cannot be described as end-to-end accelerator scheduling or full-network performance.
